ai.definition: RAG Pipelines for Knowledge Graphs are systems that integrate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques with knowledge graph structures to enhance the accuracy and relevance of generated content.
ai.howItWorks: These pipelines first retrieve information from a pre-built knowledge graph, then use this context to generate new insights or content. The retrieval step ensures that the generation process is grounded in accurate and relevant data, improving the overall quality of the output.
ai.problemSolved: The challenge of generating high-quality, contextually rich content based on complex and interconnected information sources, while maintaining accuracy and relevance.
ai.manufacturing: No specific manufacturing processes are involved; rather, these pipelines require sophisticated software development and integration with existing knowledge graph systems.
ai.buildProcess: Involves developing a robust retrieval system that can efficiently query the knowledge graph, followed by training generation models to understand and use this context effectively. The process also includes fine-tuning for specific domains or applications.
ai.costDrivers: Mainly driven by the cost of maintaining and updating the underlying knowledge graphs, as well as the computational resources required for advanced retrieval and generation algorithms.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to grow in adoption as more industries recognize the value of context-rich content generation.
ai.regulation: Currently not heavily regulated but may face future scrutiny, especially concerning data privacy and bias in generated content.
ai.risks: Potential risks include data quality issues, biases in the knowledge graph, and ethical concerns related to the use of AI-generated content.
ai.profitability: Profit potential is high due to increased demand for accurate and context-rich content across various industries, but requires significant investment in R&D and infrastructure.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving the integration between retrieval and generation, enhancing the scalability of these systems, and addressing ethical concerns related to AI-generated content.

glossary.def: A technique that combines information retrieval with natural language generation to produce contextually rich and accurate outputs.
A structured representation of entities, their attributes, and relationships between them, used for storing and querying complex knowledge.

subsystems.name: Graph construction
subsystems.role: turns documents into entities and relationships.
parts: entity and relation extraction by LLM

subsystems.name: Knowledge graph store
subsystems.role: holds the nodes, edges and their provenance.

subsystems.name: Index layer
subsystems.role: makes the graph searchable by both meaning and structure.

subsystems.name: Retrieval engine
subsystems.role: finds the right subgraph for a question.

subsystems.name: Generation and grounding
subsystems.role: answers using the retrieved subgraph and cites it.
parts: prompt assembly with triples and summaries

subsystems.name: Evaluation and maintenance
subsystems.role: keeps the graph correct and the answers faithful.

buildSteps.title: Define the schema
buildSteps.detail: Decide which entity and relationship types matter for the domain; an open schema invites noise, a rigid one misses facts.

buildSteps.title: Extract the graph
buildSteps.detail: Chunk source documents, then have a language model extract entities and relations from each chunk, with the passage recorded as evidence.

buildSteps.title: Resolve and link
buildSteps.detail: Merge duplicate entities (the same organisation written five ways) into canonical nodes, and attach each to its source spans.

buildSteps.title: Build the index
buildSteps.detail: Embed nodes and edges, cluster related nodes, and write summaries for each cluster so broad questions can be answered without full traversal.

buildSteps.title: Index queries, not just documents
buildSteps.detail: At question time, identify entities in the query, find matching graph nodes, then expand outward a few hops or to the relevant cluster.

buildSteps.title: Assemble context
buildSteps.detail: Package the retrieved triples, their source text and cluster summaries into the model prompt, ordered by relevance.

buildSteps.title: Generate with citations
buildSteps.detail: The model writes the answer, and each claim is tied back to a node, edge or document — unverifiable claims are flagged.

buildSteps.title: Operate and refresh
buildSteps.detail: Monitor grounding quality, re-extract from changed documents, and merge new nodes into the existing graph.

prerequisites.why: they do the extraction, query interpretation and final writing.

prerequisites.tech: Vector databases and approximate nearest-neighbour search
prerequisites.why: they retrieve semantically similar nodes and passages at speed.
they store triples and run multi-hop traversals.

models still miss implicit relationships and hallucinate edges unless every triple is grounded in text.

pathway.milestone: graph-augmented RAG demonstrated on narrow domains such as biomedical or enterprise document sets
pathway.unlocks: answers that require joining facts across several documents.

pathway.milestone: standardised, incremental graph building with provenance on every edge
pathway.unlocks: corpora that change daily can be trusted, not rebuilt from scratch.

pathway.milestone: structured queries over text and tabular data in one pipeline
pathway.unlocks: analyst-style questions mixing documents, spreadsheets and databases.

pathway.milestone: self-maintaining knowledge graphs that correct and merge themselves
pathway.unlocks: long-lived assistants whose knowledge stays accurate without manual curation.
